Compared with the traditional teaching method, students' enthusiasm and interest can be aroused through the iterations of "cognition, theory and realization", the students' innovative ability can be brought into play, and the feedback from students is better. Therefore, this iterative teaching method not only trains students' practical design abilities, but also strengthens students' theoretical cognition, and obviously improves the teaching effect.

articleTitle: Disease Classification Model Based on Qubit Neural Tree Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This paper introduces a quantum-inspired Qubit neural tree networks with improved Qubit neuron, overlayer connections and different phase operation functions for different neurons to construct disease classification model. A hybrid evolutionary algorithm that combines the modified PIPE algorithm with beetle antennae search is also proposed to optimize the structure and parameters of the Qubit neural tree network. Simulation results on two disease classification problems show that this model has more advantages in classification precision, feature selection and structure simplification, especially for classification with multi-class attributes.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Community Opening on Road Traffic
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the increasing number of vehicles and the saturation of urban roads, the influence of closed residential areas on urban road conditions is becoming increasingly prominent. The open residential area can optimize the road network structure and alleviate the traffic congestion by increasing the density of the road network and enhancing the traffic capacity. In this paper, a mathematical model of vehicle passage is established to study the influence of the opening of residential area on the surrounding roads. The study of road problems is analogous to the problems of circuits. The driving process of motor vehicle is compared to the process of electron transfer, and the traffic flow is compared to the magnitude of electric current. The variation of urban traffic with time is compared to the charging and discharging process of capacitors. A signal generator composed of operational amplifiers and urban network traffic is used to simulate the daily peak periods and a mathematical model based on differential equations is established.

articleTitle: Model Checking an Artificial Neural Networks System in Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the progress in science and technology, many Applications of Artificial Neural Networks in medical fields have been developing rapidly. Considering that the advent of practical service seems to be inevitable, the performance evaluation of these systems is worthy. Therefore, this paper selects one typical ANNs-based system in medical diagnosis to verify its reliability. In order to check the reliability of this system, this paper introduces a tool called PRISM with the probabilistic model checking technique. Additionally, the self learning mechanism inside the ANNs will also be simulated to discern its usefulness. Our study comprehensively digs the impact of those modules in this system and discovers the positive function of the self learning on medical diagnosis.

Author Keywords: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), Model Checking, Reliability, PRISM, Self Learning

articleTitle: A Ten-Long Non-Coding RNA Model Improves Prognosis Prediction of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Patients
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In this paper, the lncRNA expression profiles of 424 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients, including 374 tumor and 50 adjacent non-tumor tissues, from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. By univariate and multivariate Cox survival analysis, we found and validated 10 significant lncRNAs associated with HCC prognosis. Based on the risk calculation model established on these 10 lncRNAs, HCC patients samples could be divided into high-risk and low-risk groups, and the survival rates of patients in these two groups are significantly different. Our research provides data to further understand the molecular mechanisms implicated in HCC and to improve diagnosis, treatment and prognosis used for HCC patients.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Network for Point Cloud of Medicine Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Great progress has been made in 3D reconstruction of medicine structures through medical images such as CT and MRI in recent years. With the demand for virtual surgery and other technologies, it has become an important research topic that how to segment the reconstructed 3D model. 3D models are generally stored in CAD or MAX formats and need to be transformed into point clouds before they can be segmented. Our work proposed a new deep learning network structure, which can directly process irregular point cloud. Empirically, it showed competitive performance in many 3D tasks such as object classification and semantic segmentation. The trained network was applied to the reconstructed 3D models of medicine structures, and good results were also obtained.

articleTitle: A New Efficient Algorithm for Weighted Vertex Cover in Bipartite Graphs Based on a Dual Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The (un-weighted) vertex cover problem in general graphs is a classical NP-hard problem, but it is polynomial time solvable in bipartite graphs. This paper considers two combinatorial optimization problems. One is the weighted vertex cover problem and the other is the so-called maximum edge packing problem. We proved that in bipartite graphs, maximum edge packing problem can be viewed as the dual of the weighted vertex cover problem, and hence these two problems are polynomial time solvable. We explored the relationships between these two problems in bipartite graphs and some structural results are obtained accordingly. Furthermore, a new efficient algorithm for the weighted vertex cover problem in bipartite graphs is also derived. Our method generalized some previous algorithms for un-weighted vertex cover in bipartite graphs.

articleTitle: Model Checking of Systems with Unreliable Machines Using PRISM
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: A system with two machines and one buffer is common in many fields. However, the machines cannot be always stable. This paper introduces a system consisting of two unreliable machines and one buffer, which is applied in a manufacturing factory. The evaluation of its reliability and performance will be discussed using a model checking software called PRISM. The model is based on the Continuous-time Markov chain.

Author Keywords: Model checking, PRISM, Reprogramming System, CTMC

articleTitle: An Improved Tikhonov Method for Magnetic Induction Tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Magnetic induction tomography (MIT) is a non-contact and more advanced technique than CT imaging. The main reason why it is still in the laboratory research stage are that the edges of reconstructed image are blurred and cannot satisfy quality requirements. Based on this, a random boundary optimization method is proposed for MIT. The method is to optimize edge information. Firstly, we chose the Tikhonov optimization algorithm with poor boundary information, the image reconstruction result of Tikhonov is seen as the initial state. Then, through the K-means clustering theory, a binary image is produced; By using the expansion and corrosion method of mathematical morphology, the boundary information is extracted; Particle swarm optimization is used to optimize the boundary information. Finally, experiment result shows that the image error and correlation coefficient are much better than Tikhonov algorithm. So it is a kind of MIT image reconstruction method with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of SaaS Mode in Customizable Graduation Design Management System
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of multiple graduation design processes, long cycle, and difficult management, a customizable graduation design management system based on SaaS mode is designed and implemented. Multi-tenant identification, data isolation, personalized customization, system scalability technical solution will be proposed and the SaaS model multi-tenant system will be built in this paper. The multi-tenant technology is used to make the system can be shared by major universities to implement software reuse. For the non-customizable features of traditional systems, the development of component-based functional modules is proposed to make the function customized. The graduation design process is extracted as a functional module, enabling universities and colleges to modify the graduation design process and score standards according to their needs. To address the problem caused by the huge user, an application instance is expanded into multiple instances, multiple data sources are configured dynamically and the table structure is improved to achieve database scalability. The problems in the traditional graduation design process are effectively solved through the above schemes.

articleTitle: Intensity Modulated Arc Therapy (IMAT) vs. IMRT in Glottic Cancer: A Treatment Planning Comparison on Conventional Linac
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Previous advanced radiation therapy (RT) techniques for early stage glottic cancer attempted to spare the normal tissue. We aimed to evaluate the dosimetric advantages of intensity modulated arc therapy (IMAT) in terms of increase target tumor dose and sparing normal tissue hand-dose in early-stage glottic cancer patients. In our previous published paper, we explored the application of conventional linear accelerator IMAT technology in large-scale tumors of cervical cancer and elongate target areas of esophageal cancer.The purpose of this study is to investigate using constant dose rate IMAT on conventional linear accelerator, by comparing with the IMRT technology to evaluate the performance of IMAT on early-stage glottic carcinoma patients and then provide guidance for clinical treatment. The results show that glottic carcinoma can be implemented IMAT plans on conventional Linac for smoothly and quickly at busy cancer center. IMAT planning can meet the clinical demand, showed significant dosimetric benefits in sparing both the thyroid gland and carotid artery. Compared with IMRT, IMAT plan has more MUs and less treatment time and significantly improves the treatment efficiency.An evaluation of weight loss must be performed during treatment for IMAT patients.

articleTitle: User Modeling Based on Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Nowadays, there are lots of people use social media. In addition to, the social media changed the users' conversation model, that use the message to the conversation more than before. The social media can make people easy to contact other people, but it makes people face to face to communicate become less. In this situation, we want to know users' emotion, behavior when users' using social media. Because the user sends the message or writes a review that meaning is different. In this research, we use sentiment analysis to analysis text. The research data is based on the sharing economy platform. The sharing economy is a new economic model. This is need to high trust to share the house with other people. So some users have given the feedback to the provider. There are two feedback type in most of social media or websites. One is text review; another is star-rating or score. Some people will write good comments, but give a low score or star-rating for the providers. In our research, we will investigate the relationship between the text-only review and the score or star-rating.

articleTitle: Approaches to Improve Teaching Quality of Histology and Embryology by Various Ways
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Histology and embryology is an important basic medical course. Through the exploration and practice of histology and embryology teaching, we found that by integrating multiple teaching methods, integrating multi-disciplinary knowledge points, applying philosophical thinking and mind mapping, and encouraging students to participate in relevant scientific research, students can mobilize the enthusiasm of independent learning and improve the teaching quality of histology and embryology.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of E-Commerce Enterprises Soft Operating Costs Based on Exponential Smoothing Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In order to predict more accurately E-commerce enterprises soft operating costs, this paper establishes the forecasting model basing on exponential smoothing technique, finds out the optimal smoothing constant by use of Excel programming solution tool, attains the prediction value through two times smoothing analysis, and provides persuasive evidence for E-commerce enterprises to control costs.

Author Keywords: Operating Costs, Exponential Smoothing, Smoothing Constant, Predictive Analysis

articleTitle: Central Lymph Node Metastasis as a Predictor for Lateral Lymph Node Metastasis in Clinically Node-Negative T3 and T4 Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Background: To evaluate the pattern of lateral lymph node metastasis(LLNM)and the impact of central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) on lymph node resection at level II-V in clinically node-negative(cN0)T3 and T4 papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) patients. Methods: 151 patients with PTC who underwent total thyroidectomy plus bilateral central lymph node dissection (CLND) and unilateral lymph node dissection (LLND) were retrospectively reviewed. Results: We used univariate and multivariate regression analysis to investigate risk factors of LLNM and the pattern of LLNM in PTC. 1) CLNM was a risk factor for LLNM (odds ratio of 2.776). 2) The numbers of involved central lymph nodes were positively correlated with the incidence of LLNM and the number of LLNM involved regions. Conclusions: The number of central lymph nodes involved correlated with higher LLNM, total thyroidectomy plus bilateral central lymph node dissection (CLND) should be first considered for the T3 and T4 PTC patients in which we recommended modified radical cervical lymph nodes dissection to remove the ipsilateral level II-V lymph nodes.

Author Keywords: papillary thyroid carcinoma, lymph node metastasis, risk factors, neck dissection

articleTitle: Deep Feature Learning Based Clustering with Application to TCM Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Clustering analysis is an important unsupervised learning method for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) data analysis. Due to the variance and heterogeneity of TCM data, features extracted directly from the input space may lead to poor clustering results. With the success of deep learning study and applications, we propose a feature learning framework based on deep network models to improve the quality of the learned features. The proposed framework incorporates deep feature learning and clustering leading to a global optimization solution. The proposed method is applied to two TCM clinical datasets and the results indicate that the proposed method is superior to the current state-of-the-art methods.

Author Keywords: TCM data analysis, clustering, deep feature learning, unsupervised learning

articleTitle: Security and Design Analysis of Certificateless Signature Schemes as Teaching Cases of Cryptography and Security Course Education
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: More and more security and privacy issues have been exposed which lead to the urgent requirement of solving the security and privacy. Many universities and colleges offer the course education of cryptography and security and make it be an important compulsory course. However, cryptography as the key technology of solving security and privacy is very theoretical and very hard to be mastered by the students. In this paper, we use the hot cryptosystem - certificateless signature scheme as the teaching case. By adopting two current certificateless signature schemes, we analyze the existing design and security problems of these two certificateless signature schemes in cryptography course education. We give the details attacking process of forging a valid certificateless signature without known the signer's private key. In the same time, we analyze these problems and present some simple improvement methods. By using case teaching, it can make the student easier and better master the cryptosystem in cryptography course education.

articleTitle: Research on Data Integration Based on Kettle
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Kettle is a powerful ETL tool for data integration. We implement kettle in the data integration and sharing of the basic database. The key issues of ETL implementation include multi-data source data consolidation and data incremental update. We put forward the “merge join” and “database join” solutions for multi-data source data consolidation and the “timestamps”, “triggers”, “Database log data” and “Data comparison” solution for data incremental update issue.

articleTitle: Development of Interactive Experimental Teaching Platform for Workshop Layout Simulation Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Workshop layout design has attracted wide attention of researchers, and there are relatively mature theories and methods for it. However, because of the frontier of bionic algorithm and the difficulty of integration with simulation technology, the experimental teaching methods in workshop layout design technology are still lacking. For the problem above, based on the establishment of the mathematical model of workshop layout design, an experimental teaching platform for workshop layout simulation was developed by combining genetic algorithm with advanced simulation technology. Through this platform, interactive layout optimization and simulation can be parameterized. Consequently students can achieve a deep understanding of the relationship between the parameters and the performance of the algorithm, and get the experiment learning effect of the mastery of the theory and method for workshop layout.

Author Keywords: interactive experimental teaching, machine layout problem, simulation teaching platform, job shop, genetic algorithm

articleTitle: Effects of Clothing Pressure on Blood Circulation During Gymnastics Sport
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study the effects of clothing pressure on blood circulation during gymnastics sports. First, the values of pressure and blood circulation in static and dynamic states were measured on 8 young females with body size similar to the standard body. Then the change rate of Blood Velocity and Blood Flow were found under dynamic states significantly increased. At the same time, using SPSS software suggested that the change rate of Blood Velocity and Blood Flow are affected by pressure. The pressure of the gymnastics tights, Blood Velocity and Blood Flow are positively correlated. The pressure of text sites, Blood Velocity and Blood Flow are positively related. At last it helps to use blood circulation indexes as an important criterion to evaluate clothing comfort.

articleTitle: The Online Medical Physics Curriculum-Group-Construction Under the Background of Modernization of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Emerging Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Both Modernization of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Emerging Engineering Education require training comprehensive and innovative talents. In universities of traditional Chinese medicine, medical physics must play a role as a bridge link between the traditional Chinese medicine and the high-technology. In view of the decreasing class hours of physics courses, a multidimensional and interactive online medical physics curriculum-group-construction mode is proposed. In combination with the requirements of the times and the educational goals of our university, we explore the mode of the online medical physics curriculum-group-construction, including the construction of multi-dimensional learning environment, the orientation and modular design of the curriculum-group, and the construction of high-quality learning content.

articleTitle: Empirical Study of Project Teaching Based on Combining Learning with Working
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, the training of network programming skills is one of the core objectives of the applied university network engineering teaching, and how to improve the students' active participation, cooperation between teachers and students, exploration and innovation are the key problems encountered in the process of university education. Aiming at these problems, this article is based on project teaching mode to train students of network engineering specialty in programming skill training and programming ability. By analyzing the requirements and knowledge points of the course, drawing on the idea of combining work with engineering, taking the project group as the form of teaching organization, it has realized a project teaching mode management with the guidance of teachers, students' independent learning as the core, and the whole process of project through the whole process of teaching. Taking "network programming" as an example, this paper proves that the application of this teaching mode can arouse students' learning interest and improve students' comprehensive professional quality.

Author Keywords: project teaching, combining learning with working, network programming, evaluation system

articleTitle: Exploration of Research-Oriented Microbiology Teaching Model: Taking Mycobacteriophage Isolation as Example
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In medical school, pathogenic microorganism experiment course is a crucial practical course needing operation. There are amounts of barrier in the practical teaching design and specific implementation of the course. To a certain extent, it has affected and hindered the realization of favorable teaching results. A useful way of solving these problems is to adopting the optimum teaching methods on the basis of a comprehensive analysis of the course itself and students' situations. Under the guidance of the primary line of analyzing, discovering and resolving problems, this paper held a discussion on the teaching methods that can effectively enhance the teaching effect of pathogenic microorganism experiment course.

articleTitle: Humanoid Soft Hand Design Based on sEMG Control
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Based on the design of the human hand and driving theory, a humanoid soft manipulator with three cavities structure is proposed, and the three-dimensional model of the soft manipulator is modeled. The large deformation mathematical model of the soft manipulator is established by using Yeoh model. Combined with the geometrical relation between the deformation and the Kraiberian equation, the relationship among the input pressure, geometric parameters and bending angle were analyzed. According to the finite element analysis, the influence of the number of cavities, the shape of the cavity side, the pressure in the cavity and the direct punching on the bending performance of the soft manipulator were obtained. The structure of the humanoid robot and its pneumatic system were designed and fabricated. Based on the characteristics of the surface EMG (sEMG) of the muscle group, the ten kinds of gesture recognition and control modes were established, and the real-time control of the soft-manipulator was realized by the EMG signal. The robot can reproduce the gesture behavior of the person, the recognition rate is 93.2%. The conclusion can provide theoretical support for the development of humanoid soft manipulator.

Author Keywords: EMG, Soft robot, Three-stage cavity, Finite element analysis, Man-machine interaction

articleTitle: Innovative Teaching Practice of Integrated Computer Courses with Focus on Students' System Ability
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In recent years, computer technology has developed rapidly especially the reconfigurable computing devices and related technology. This makes the related computer courses are confronted with an enormous challenge. With great importance attached to cultivating students' system ability, this paper makes teaching researches using EDA technologies through application of both software and hardware then apply them to the actual teaching practice. The courses are organized as the course group which can be extended through adding related courses for aimed major. And at the same time we have established a systematic and progressive experiment system. Consequently, students can deepen their understanding of the computer system, improve their ability to address practical problems and thus develop their over-all ability.

articleTitle: Model Checking Denial-of-Service Attack Against IEEE 802.15.6 Protocol
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the prevalence of Internet of Things, numerous system vulnerabilities can be explored, and the hacker may launch a series of DoS attacks by exploiting the vulnerabilities of the system. In this paper, a simulation experiment is designed to implement DoS attacks on a system that utilizes the IEEE 802.15.6 password association protocol to accomplish the information transmission. During the process, authors introduce the probabilistic model checking technique with the tool of PRISM. This method is used for the analysis of the factors affecting the success rate of DoS attacks. The study is expected to enrich the analysis of the factors influencing the success rate of DoS attacks.

articleTitle: A Study of the Reading Behavior of University Students
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Reading is part of our daily life. For university students, reading is extremely important for improving their professional knowledge and cultivating their personal hobbies. This work studied the relationship between the university students' academic ranking and their reading behavior as well as reading quantities. By analyzing the data of library loan records and the examination performances of all the students who majored in software engineering in Chang'an University within their four-year-long undergraduate study, we set the reading quantities of professional books and other (non-professional) books as two essential factors, and established a model based on multiple linear regression machine learning algorithm, which successfully predicted the students' academic ranking from their reading quantities. K-means was also used to perform simple clustering on different types of students.

articleTitle: The Influence of Dunqiang Qigong on Hearing and Blood Sugar Lever of Patients with Diabetes Deafness
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective To observe the influence of Dunqiang Qigong on hearing and blood sugar lever of patients with diabetes deafness. Methods 70 patients with diabetes mellitus (NIDDM) with deafness, were randomly divided into two groups, treatment group 39 cases (61 ears), control group of 31 cases (54 ears). Treatment group practice Dunqiang Qigong and eat Glenn urea every other day. Control group every day Glenn urea and conventional medicines of treating deafness. The hearing, FBG, PBG, and 24h urine sugar quantitative changes were observed in two groups before and after treatment. Results Total effective rate of hearing improved in the treatment group was 31.6%, the control group was 29.6% (p>0.05).The change of fasting blood glucose(FBG), 2h postprandial blood glucose(PBG) and 24h urine glucose quantitative were more obvious than those before treatment in two groups(P<;0.05, P<;0.01), Among them,the curative effect of PBG and 24h urine sugar quantitmive in treatment group were better than those of control group (p<;0.01), FBG has no obvious difference in two groups(p>0.05). Conclusion Dunqiang Qigong can change blood glucose and hearing of patients with diabetes deaf and reduce the amount of diabetes drugs.

articleTitle: Promotion of College Students' Physical Health: A Case Study on Physical Education Intervention
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: There are a number of variables that affect the college students' physical health. The level of college students' physical health has been declining for many years, improving the physical quality of students is an important task of higher physical education. The current study was conducted to investigate the contributions of physical education intervention to college students' physical health. Selected students of Wuhan University of Technology (N=6533) in grade 2014 as samples, through the implementation of teaching intervention, observation and comparison analysis of health test indexes is conducted before and after intervention. Using literature review, expert consultation, measurement and mathematical statistics and other research methods, study on the feasibility of improving the physical health of college students by the teaching intervention of X+ physical quality. The results show that: physical education teaching can effectively improve the physical quality of students, including the improvement of physical fitness of boys is significantly higher than girls.

articleTitle: A Segmentation Framework for MR Images Combining with Tissue Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance (MR) brain tissue segmentation plays an important role in assisting diagnosis, treatment planning and surgical navigation. In this paper, a framework combining with T1 mapping is proposed to segment white matter (WM), gray matter (GM) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). For the T1 parameters are intrinsic MR properties of tissue, it can be used as prior knowledge for MR images segmentation. The pro-posed framework is mainly divided into two parts: one is T1 mapping acquisition and preprocessing, another is prediction and reclassification of mislabeled voxels based on support vector machine (SVM). Evaluated by Dice coefficient, the experiment results are significantly improved above 15 percent for brain tissue segmentation. In a conclusion, T1 mapping can be seen as objective prior information for MR images segmentation.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Method for Urban Travel Time Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: An accurate time prediction of a path is of great importance to route planning and navigations. With the widespread use and popularity of the Global Positioning System (GPS), it is possible to collect massive vehicle trajectories for travel time prediction. However, most existing travel time prediction approaches are segment-based methods, which are not accuracy as they are not able to capture many cross-segment factors. In this paper, we propose a unique feature extraction structure which takes multiple features into account. Besides, we also use ensemble method to predict travel time which can take advantage of every single model strength. A series of experiments have been conducted on real datasets, the result demonstrates that MFPEL outperforms over existing approaches.

articleTitle: Application and Evaluation of Diversified Teaching Mode in the Practice Classes of Oral Histopathology
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective: To explore the application effect of diversified teaching mode in the practice classes of oral histopathology. Methods: The effect of teaching was evaluated through closed-book examination and questionnaire. Results: The exam scores in diversified teaching mode group were superior to those in traditional teaching group. The evaluation of students to diversified teaching mode is higher than that of traditional teaching mode, especially in the aspect of learning interest, learning ability and communication between teachers and students. Conclusion: The diversified teaching mode has received good results in the practical teaching of oral histopathology, which has aroused the initiative and enthusiasm of students and cultivated their comprehensive ability.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Techniques for Fall Detection in Geriatric Healthcare Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Intelligent IoT-based ambient assisted living systems (AALS) have been a major research focus area in recent times. According to the studies conducted by National Program for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE), elderly population in India will increase to 12% of the national population by 2025 with 8%-10% requiring utmost care. Application of machine learning in areas of AALS such as fall detection, therefore, has the potential to have huge public impact. In this paper, we propose a fall detection system that takes into account not only various wearable sensor node parameter readings for a subject, but also his biological and physiological profile. The profile is used to determine a fall risk category for the subject. We performed machine learning experiments using public datasets for fall detection which included wearable sensor node readings. The algorithms were then retrained by feeding in the risk categorization of the subject, and results from this analyses are presented. The objective of the experiments was to find out the impact of a subject's risk categorization on the accuracy of fall detection. The algorithms presented here form part of a comprehensive geriatric healthcare system under development, which comprises wearable sensor nodes, co-ordinator nodes, an indoor localization framework and cloud-hosted application servers. A brief overview of the system capabilities is also presented.

articleTitle: Top-k Structure Holes Detection Algorithm in Social Network
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In the research of social networks, the structure holes usually refers to the vertices in the network at the key positions of information diffusion. The detection of such vertices is of great significance for the control of network public opinion, the analysis of the influence of social network, the detection of the weak points of the network security, the rapid spread of the information and so on. How to find more accurate structural holes has become a key problem in the research. In this paper, we proposed a method to detect the top-k structure holes based on the shortest path increment. It mainly through the analysis of SPIG (the shortest path increment), NCC (the number of sub connected components) and VAR (the variance of the vertices in a connected component) to determine the structure hole attribute values of the vertices. And then the vertices are sorted according to this value and obtained the top-k vertices. Our experiments on real networks and different scales LFR simulation complex networks clearly verify the effectiveness of our method, as well as the advantage of our method against the other similar methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Virtual Experimental Platform for Power System Teaching
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The education of power system automation and control is a very important element of the industrialization process in developing countries. However, traditional experimental equipment requires a significant budget in promotion. And it mainly includes hardware devices, which have a lot of limitations in the laboratory field, extensibility, comprehensiveness and practical teaching efficiency. This paper gives a detailed description of a virtual experimental platform for power system teaching (VEPS) based on object-oriented thinking, aiming to help users such as undergraduate students and researchers to realize the basic dynamic process of power system. The simulation modules of VEPS include under frequency load shedding (UFLS), excitation control (EC), parallel control (PC) and complex power system operation (CPSO). The VEPS achieves the visualization of real-time, time-series dynamic simulation and comparative analysis mode (CAM) of the power system, allowing students to set operation modes, system models and parameters to ensure flexi-bility and openness of the experiment. Key issues of the platform, such as system architecture, experimental contents and promo-tion effect in college are emphatically discussed.

articleTitle: Bioinformatics Analysis on Potential Anti-Viral Targets Against Spike Protein of MERS-CoV
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective Middle East respiratory syndrome is caused by the Middle respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and the mortality is high. However, to date, there is no effective vaccine or antibody for human immunity and treatment as a putative therapeutic agent specific for MERS. The aim of this study was to obtain the bioinformatic characteristics of the MERS-CoV S protein antigen. Methods SOPMA Server software and the DiscoTope were used to predict the secondary and tertiary structures of the MERS-CoV S protein, respectively, whilst a number of online prediction software applications, including IEDB, Syfpeithi and other resources of IEDB, were used for the T- and B-cell epitope predictions. Results The prediction results indicated that the T-cell epitopes were located at positions 950-958, 317-325, 1309-1317, 480-488 and 388-396, whereas the B-cell epitopes were located at positions 520-528, 629-637, 659-667, 734-744, 1205-1212. 19-53, 300-309, 478-523, 528-550 and 622-632. Conclusion These regions were the potential dominant epitopes of the MERS-CoV S protein antigen. The results of our study provide experimental data for the identification and screening of epitopes and may be used for the development of epitope vaccines that have an enhanced safety and efficacy. This may result in the provision of improved regimens for the prevention and treatment of MERS.

articleTitle: Feature-Based Dividing Symbolic Time Series Representation for Streaming Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Along with the continuous development of infor- mation technology, massive numbers of detecting instruments or systems in various fields are continuously producing plenty number of streaming time series data. In recent years, many representation approaches for time series has been proposed with the main objective of dimensionality reduction to support various data mining algorithms in the domain of time series data processing. Symbolic Aggregate approXimation(SAX) is a major symbolic representation and dimensionality reduction algorithm which has been widely used in many application scenarios of time series data mining, such as motifs discov- ery,outlier detection, etc. In this paper, we propose a symbolic representation method of streaming time series based on VTP- diving with sliding window and a similarity measurement algorithm for the proposed representation method which lower bounding the Euclidean distance on the original data. Extensive experiments on different kinds of typical time series datasets have been conducted to demonstrate the advantages of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Prediction of Postpartum Hemorrhage by Adaptive K-Nearest Neighbor Based on Influence Factors
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: For the binary classification problems that the available values for all feature attributesin the dataset are discrete conventional, K-Nearest Neighbor(KNN) considers that the distances between different feature attribute values are the same when calculating the distance between the predicted sample and the training sample, which is not consistent with the actual situation. In this paper, we proposed an algorithm named Adaptive K-Nearest Neighbor Based on Influence Factors (AKNN-IF) which solved the disadvantages of KNN algorithm in calculating the distance of discrete conventional feature attributes. Moreover, as the size of the dataset grows, the influence factors will reflect the degree of the influence more realistically of different feature attribute values on label attributes and it's more effective to use influence factors to calculate the distance of different feature attribute values. Meanwhile, the impact of imbalanced data on the classification effect is weakened. As the influence factor is obtained through self-learning of the data, no human intervention is required, so that the algorithm has a certain self-adaptability. We tested some data which contained 1829 samples and proved that the classification effect of the AKNNIF algorithm is superior to the KNN algorithm, SVM, and C4.5 for the binary classification problems in which all the feature attributes are discrete conventional. AKNN-IF can contribute to the prevention and control of postpartum hemorrhage.

articleTitle: Predicting Carbonylation Sites of Human Proteins with a New Max-Significance and Min-Redundancy Feature Selection Criterion
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Protein carbonylation is a typical oxidative stress-induced post-translational modification (PTM), which has an important role in proteasome activity and cellular dysfunctions. Mass spectrometry is one of the most common ways to analyze protein carbonyl level and identify exact modification sites. It has been found that four types of amino acid residues, including lysine (K), arginine (R), threonine (T) and proline (P), are prone to carbonylation. However, these experimental approaches are not suitable for batch processing of proteins, and the predictive power of existing relevant bioinformatical tools are still weak. In the paper, an improved method with a new max-significance and min-redundancy (MSAMR) feature selection criterion was proposed to predict human carbonylation sites. This method can achieve total accuracies of 87.43%, 86.83%, 86.56% and 88.10% for K, R, T and P carbonylation site predictions respectively using 10-fold cross-validation. Different kinds of features involved in the method, especially a new kind of customized amino acid composition (CAAC) features, were analyzed, and the performance of MSAMR feature selection criterion was discussed. Furthermore, a software tool CarSPred2.0 was released to serve for human carbonylation site prediction.All datasets and the software can be available at https://github.com/lhqxinghun/bioinformatics/tree/master/CarSPred-2.0/.

Author Keywords: Oxidative stress, Predicting human carbonylation sites, Max-significance and min-redundancy, CarSPred

articleTitle: Development of an Undergraduate Control Engineering Design Project: PID Control of Blood Glucose Levels in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus Subjects
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Considerations in the development of a simulation-based (matlab/SIMULINK) undergraduate Control Engineering project are outlined. The main objective of the simulation-based project, which will run in parallel with the first part of the control course, is to further embed in the students, the basic concepts of modelling, feedback control, feedforward control and performance assessment of the controlled system. The `tuning' of the parameters of a proportional, integral and derivative (PID) controller to obtain a desired controlled performance is an important element of the project. The specific application considered is the post-prandial control of blood glucose levels in type I diabetes Mellitus subjects using insulin. Worldwide numbers of diabetes sufferers are steadily increasing around the world putting a strain on both healthcare resources and costs. Choosing an application of global significance does create an increased level of student engagement to the Control Engineering project.

articleTitle: A Feature-Enhanced Entity Recognition Method for Chinese Electronic Medical Records
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Electronic medical records (EMRs) contain rich medical information, which is of great significance to medical research. The amount of Chinese EMRs is growing, whereas the current named entity recognition methods based on machine learning do not consider the unique characteristics of Chinese EMR. In this paper, four types of entities for disease, symptom, inspection and treatment are trained and tested using the conditional random field model. Firstly, tag-of-words, part-of-speech and context are selected as the basic features. Secondly, by analyzing the characteristics of Chinese electronic medical record text, the chapter name feature, core word feature and word clustering feature are selected as the extended features. Among them, the core word feature is obtained by dividing the collected dictionary into characters and words and then counting the character frequency and word frequency. The word vector clustering feature is obtained by clustering word vectors. Then, by constructing a medical dictionary, a semi-automatic corpus annotation method is used to randomly extract and classify the corpora of a certain scale. Finally, using the conditional random field tool CRF++ to learn and predict, it achieves an accuracy of 93.03%, a recall rate of 90.69%, and an F value of 91.85%.

Author Keywords: Chinese electronic medical records, named entity recognition, feature enhancing, CRF

articleTitle: An Ontology-Based Approach to Double Scenario Model Knowledge Base Development for International Disaster Relief
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Research Purpose: To establish a knowledge base for the double scenario model which involve large interdisciplinary knowledge. Propose Methods: This research established a conceptual scenario model with two different levels of ambition: a disaster scenario, in which casualty figure, composition of injuries are constrained by the types of the disaster as well as the degree of the damage, and a country scenario, in which the healthcare needs are constrained by the health coverage and the health condition of local people. Because of the multidisciplinary and professional characteristic of disaster relief, this research uses ontology technology to solve the problem of knowledge expressing, sharing and reusing. This method was used to describe the hierarchical structure and the relation rules of the concept and terms related to the model. Thus, we could structure the cases of international medical relief and establish the knowledge base. Based on the knowledge base, we could realize the function of similarity match and data inquire. As well as decision assistant function. Results and Conclusion: This article uses the armed conflicts in Syrian Arab Republic and Yemen as examples. The comparing results show that the outcomes of the double-level scenario model fit this reality

articleTitle: Relationship Between Air Pollutants and Outpatient Visits for Respiratory Diseases in Hangzhou
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This paper evaluated the impact of major air pollutants on respiratory diseases quantitatively and predicted the number of short-term outpatient visits in Hangzhou in China. A semi-parametric generalized additive model (GAM) was used to analyse the relationship between the air pollutants and the number of daily reporting cases of respiratory diseases. The back propagation (BP) neural networks model was used to predict the number of hospital outpatients with respiratory diseases. Results showed that: 1) When PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>, PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>, NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> increased by an inter-quartile range(IQR), the relative risk(RR) of respiratory diseases is 1.030 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.016-1.045), 1.063 (95% CI: 1.043-1.084), 1.053 (95% CI: 1.016-1.091) and 1.025 (95% CI: 1.003-1.048); 2) There was a positive correlation between PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>, PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> and the incidence of respiratory diseases, which the air pollutants SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> have a lag effect on respiratory diseases with three days and four days respectively; 3) The BP neural networks model exhibited a good performance with an average relative error of 13.821%. These findings demonstrate that different pollutants have different effects on health and the hospitalization rate of daily respiratory disease is on the rise with the increase of pollutant concentration.

articleTitle: Topology Analysis of Learning Cognitive Flow for Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In recent years, improving the level of personalized education has attracted research interest of a great amount of people. However, it is difficult to make the high dimensional cognitive learning space visible, computational and controllable. Whats more, manual data collection is difficult to meet the quantity and accuracy requirements, bringing obstacles in observing more accurate learning activities and collect more effective information. In this paper, a cognitive frame for observing the learning activities based on human-computer coupling is designed, for instance a vectorization technique for the situation of learning of human-computer is provided. Firstly, based on new cognitive philosophy such as cognitive distribution and extension, we propose a general topology of learning cognitive flow for human-computer interaction, composing of an evolving and high-dimensional system. The cognitive objects and their relationships are in an implicit learning, namely, cognitive space is in a human-computer coupling state.Those are distributed and extended to an information space, so as to form a “brain cognitive body-situation of coupling-manifold of information”, which is a combination of cognition and information, named “BSM” structure. Furthermore, the mechanism for the BSM coupling morphism is analyzed, and the principle for the coupled observation of objects in a cognitive or learning manifold is proposed. At the same time, based on the concepts of category theory, such as commutative diagram and topology, a tree topology is selected as the topological structure of a low-dimensional learning space to process the observations of online learning. Finally, a special system for teaching is programmed to observe learning and training processes, thus summarizing knowledge points automatically to replace the manual way. The application of system will enable the teacher to better grasp students status of cognitive structure obviously, providing services to teaching. A new application framework for learning and a new idea for the scientific studies on learning are provided, supporting for“artificial education” to “human-computer learning” effectively.

Author Keywords: Manifold topologies, Category and morphism, Cognitive structure, Complex network, Human-computer interaction

articleTitle: iNOS Via Peroxynitrite Overformation Mediates Aortic Endothelial Injury in Diabetic Rats
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective Oxidative stress is an important mechanism in the development of chronic complications in diabetes mellitus, and endothelial injury plays a key role in the pathogenesis of diabetic vascular injury. The present study was to investigate the role of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) induced peroxynitrite (ONOO-) in the aortic endothelial injury of diabetic rats.Methods/Results: Using RT-PCR, the mRNA of iNOS and nitrotyrosine (NT), a specific marker of ONOO-, were showed a significantly increased in the aortic endothelial diabetic rats, which was induced by streptozocin (STZ) and its increased protein content and distribution level were identified by Western blot and immunohistochemistry, respectively. Light microscope (hematocylin-eosin staining) and electron microscope (scanning and transmission) were employed to observe the morphological damage including nuclear shedding, mitochondria injury and inflammatory cell infiltration. We also measured the biochemical indicators of the diabetic rats, and the content of malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), iNOS, endothelin (ET), and thromboxane B2 (TXB2) were increased and superoxide dismutase (SOD) was decreased. Conclusion: This study clarified that iNOS and its resultant exaggerated ONOO- formation, and this may play a key role in aortic endothelial injury of the diabetic rats. Thus, anti-iNOS maybe a potential therapy to prevent the ONOO- mediated oxidative stress injury.

Author Keywords: Inducible nitric oxide synthase, Peroxynitrite, Aortic endothelial lesion, Diabetic vasculopathy

articleTitle: Optimization of Ultrasonic-Assisted Extraction of Polysaccharides from Trichosanthin and Antioxidant Activities in Vitro
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Trichosanthin (TCS) is a Chinese herbal medicinal that has shown hepatoprotective effects with anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidants, and antiviral activity. The objective of this study is to optimized the ultrasonic-assisted extraction of polysaccharides from TCS and then studied the antioxidant capacity of the extracted polysaccharides. On the basis of single factor experiments, the Box-Behnken experiment analyzed and optimized the ultrasonic-assisted extraction of polysaccharides from TCS by response surface methodology. The antioxidant activity of the extract's polysaccharides was then determined including the DPPH free radicals and scavenging activities against hydroxyl (·OH), superoxide anion (·O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup>) and total antioxidant reactivity. The optimum conditions upon ultrasonic extraction were as follows: ultrasonic temperature 52 °C, ultrasonic time 44 min and water-to-material ratio 23 ml/g. Under optimum conditions, the extraction of the polysaccharides was 9.37 ± 0.45 mg/g. There were significant differences in total antioxidant reactivity, superoxide anion resistance reactivity, hydroxyl radical resistance reactivity, and the contents of polysaccharides. The ultrasound-assisted extraction saves time and offers higher extraction yield. In addition, the polysaccharides from TCS have significant antioxidant activity in vitro.

articleTitle: Researches on Modeling Learners' Collaboration Network in Virtual Learning Community
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the rapid development of online education, virtual learning community has a great impact on people's learning. Here we focus on the dynamics evolution law of collaborative behavior, characterizing the features of collaborative behaviors among learners in virtual learning community. We construct a learners' collaboration network model in virtual learning community. We analyze important statistics of the network such as the degree distribution, the average path length, the clustering coefficients. On this basis, we describe the network features and study the topology characteristics of the collaborative relationship network deeply. The experiments show that the learners' collaboration network model could depict the characteristics of virtual learning community and the characteristics of the collaborative behavior among learners more accurately. The research could enrich the existing network model construction theory, and provide the network structure foundation for the study of collaborative relationship between learners in virtual learning community.

articleTitle: Will TV White Spaces Increase Telehealth Capability?
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Realizing `totally connected healthcare' is probably the most important step towards providing both high quality and cost effective patient treatment in the future. Home-based sensing, wearable medical devices and tele-consultation will all contribute to providing continuous health monitoring, evaluation and treatment. A major obstacle will be Quality of Service within an already overcrowded frequency spectrum. The unlicensed use of TV White Spaces, frequency bands that act as buffers between licensed Digital Terrestrial Television bands, has been proposed as one approach to helping alleviate the `spectrum crunch'. UHF TV White Spaces also bring propagation advantages over conventional Wi-Fi potentially realising relatively low-cost broadband in remote areas which will greatly benefit the uptake of rural telehealth. This contribution provides an introduction to the use of TVWS, the evolution of IEEE standards to address its usage and current healthcare-based TVWS developments and challenges.

articleTitle: Inference of Gene Regulations Between Multiple Activators/Inhibitors and Singular Genes
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: A gene regulatory relation often has multiple activators or inhibitors. But most of current methods only focus on inferring gene regulatory relationships between two genes. We developed a new qualitative method for representing dynamic gene regulatory relations, and algorithms for identifying gene regulations with multiple regulators. All the algorithms are implemented in a program called GeneNetFinder (http://wilab.inha.ac.kr/genenetfinder) and tested on several gene expression data. The approach and the program would be useful for identifying gene regulations with multiple activator/inhibitors.

articleTitle: One Patient, Two Patient, Three Patient, Four - When Patients Are Counted, But Not Accounted For: Pseudoreplication In Medicine
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Background: Pseudoreplication is a statistical error occurring when treatments are not replicated or replicates are not statistically independent. Description and explanation of pseudoreplication is absent from medical literature. There are four types of pseudoreplication: simple, temporal, implicit, and pooling. Methods: The present article reviews the occurrence of type I errors caused by pseudoreplication in prominent medical journals. Fifty articles, ten randomly chosen from five prominent journals: JAMA, BMJ, The New England Journal of Medicine, The Lancet, and The Annals of Internal Medicine, were analyzed for the occurrence of pseudoreplication, and in particular which statistical comparison was utilized most resulting in this error. The unit of analysis was the article for group assessments and the statistical test within each article for comparisons. Multivariate analyses were carried out to determine the correlation of pseudoreplication type with parameters in the manuscript. Results: A total of 1,294 statistical comparisons of different hypotheses were assessed, averaging 25.9 (SE=4.2) per article. Pseudoreplication occurred an average of 37.38% (SE=5.0) per statistic utilized in studies. Temporal pseudoreplication occurred most frequently. Temporal and implicit pseudoreplication were significantly related to the first statistic (F=3.45, df=6,43, P<0.007 and F=5.32, df=6,43, P<0.0004, respectively) and simple pseudoreplication was significantly related to the second statistic utilized, F=2.81, df=5,44, P<0.03. The number of M.D.’s on a study was significantly related to pseudoreplication as determined by Roy's Largest Root = 1.2, F=2.18, df=13,23, P<0.05. Conclusions: Pseudoreplication is a serious statistical problem related to the improper implementation and analysis of statistics. Physicians and medical scientists need to be cognizant of the manner in which the error occurs to prevent Type I error.

Author Keywords: Assumptions, Pseudoreplication, Errors, Replicates, Samples, Unit of Analysis

articleTitle: Study on Blended Learning Under Background of Emerging Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: One focus of Emerging Engineering Education is the new mode of talent training. This paper studies the blended learning which combines face-to-face traditional learning and e-learning on line in one Sino-foreign cooperation program in running schools. The related computer-aided instruction theories, blended learning models and strategies, technological advances in blended learning are investigated in the paper. A case study in Information Security of Technology course is presented to verify the effectiveness of the new pedagogical strategy.

articleTitle: ECUE: An Edge Computing System for University Education
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the application of cloud computing technology, latency and resource overheads have become the major restriction factors. The university education system has the characteristics of large number of users, strong real-time requirements, and high security. This paper proposes an edge computing system framework for university education, which includes the infrastructure layer, the resource management layer and the data support layer in order to provide hardware support, management of computing resource and storage resource, and security control respectively. Moreover, it has the multi-dimensional and multi-granular analysis function for teaching data, which can serve for teachers and students. The resource management algorithms and framework presented in this paper help to make full use of the resources in the system to meet the requirements of response time, energy consumption and security, and improve the effects of teaching and learning.

Author Keywords: edge computing, university education, resource management

articleTitle: A Mobile Tool for Interactive Visualisation of Genomics Data
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Advancement in genomic research and technology has significantly improved our understandings of biology, health, and medicine. Genomics data are very complex and contain genotype and phenotype information. Health researchers have long known that many diseases such as cancer are hereditary. Gaining insight and understanding of such data would enable a better understanding of the correlation between genes and diseases, which could facilitate personalised treatment for the patients. Visualisations have been increasingly used to break the complexity of genomics data to guide better decisions. Unfortunately, research works on interactive visualisations of the genomics data on mobile devices and immersive platforms are still limited. This paper presents a new interactive visualisation and navigation of genomics data on the mobile platform. The visualisation provides an overview of the entire patient cohort in a 3D similarity-space environment as well as 2D detail views of genes of interests. We introduce a new algorithm that enables effective touch-based interaction and exploration of large number of items on small mobile screens. We illustrate the effectiveness of our platform through a childhood cancer dataset, B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL) as well as a pilot qualitative study with the domain experts.

Author Keywords: Genomic data, Mobile, 3D visualisation, Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia, Multidimensional data

articleTitle: Study on the Internationalization of Standards Bodies: Based on the Strategy Evolution of BSI
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: British Standards Institution, or BSI, is the national standards organization of the United Kingdom, shouldering the responsibility to fulfill the demands of all relevant sides with their interests, e.g. society, all levels of governments, enterprises, and the public; meanwhile, the group is indispensable in developing British standards and integrating international ones. This paper reviewed the operating pattern of national standards and the advancement of BSI, adopted balanced scorecards and strategy maps in the filed of strategic management, which is base on objective and subjective aspects was introduced. Gathered annual reports between 2013 and 2016 from the organization's official website and selected 14 performance indicators to appraise the development of BSI. It has been found, based on the strategic analysis, that the focus of BSI in the previous 5 years has all included the task of identifying the group's position in the trend of globalization, so as to improve the organization's participation into international affairs, which has been its long-range strategic plan since 1998.

articleTitle: Study on Post-Earthquake Evacuation Model by Fusing Relationship Grouping and Herd Behavior
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Emergency evacuation after the earthquake is a vital means to prevent and reduce casualties, and has important practical significance. “Grouping behavior” is relatively common in crowd evacuation. That is, the evacuees must gather together with close-knit individuals before conducting collective evacuation. Therefore, by researching the herd behavior in the evacuated population after combining the ideas of firefly algorithm, the improved social force model by fusing relationship grouping and herd behavior are proposed, which is used to simulate the flow of people. The results show that the model can simulate the group phenomenon in the crowd evacuation more accurately. Moreover, it is found that the total evacuation time of the population is longer significantly with the augment of small-scale herd in the crowd. Thus the study provides a theoretical basis for large-scale population evacuation.

articleTitle: Influence of Five-Element Music Therapy on Expression of CaMKII in Hippocampi in Rats with Post-Stroke Depression
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective: To explore the influence of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) five-element music therapy on the expression of type II Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase (CaMK-II) in calmodulin signal pathway in cerebral hippocampus tissues in rats with post-stroke depression (PSD), so as to explain the action mechanism of five-element music therapy in the treatment of PSD. Methods: A total of 40 male SD rats with body mass of (220 ± 30) g were selected as study subjects and randomized into normal group, PSD model group, music therapy group, music therapy + acupuncture group and Fluoxetine group, 8 rats in each group. After one week of adaptive feed, PSD models were made. The treatment started on post-molding d19. Music therapy group and music therapy + acupuncture group were treated for 7 days as one cycle, with 2 days of rest between treatment cycles, for consecutive 2 cycles, while Fluoxetine group was treated with continuous gavage since start of treatment, qd, until the end of treatment. Hippocampus tissues were collected from rats' brains, after which quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) was used to detect the expression of CaMKIIgene, while western blot (WB) to detect the expression of CaMKIIprotein in rats' hippocampi. Results: Relative to normal group, model group was evidently lower in expression of CaMKIIgene and protein (P<;0.01). Relative to model group, music therapy + acupuncture group and Fluoxetine group were prominently higher in the expression of CaMKIIgene (P<;0.05), and music therapy group, music therapy + acupuncture group and Fluoxetine group were notably higher in the expression of CaMKII protein (P<;0.05). Conclusion: Five-element music therapy can increase the expression of CaMKIIgene and promote the expression of CaMKII protein in hippocampi of PSD rats, while five-element music therapy concomitant with acupuncture is more superior to single five-element music therapy in clinical efficacy.

Author Keywords: Post-stroke depression, depression, five-element music therapy, acupuncture, CaMKII

articleTitle: Application of Python Programming Methods in the Constructing of Effective Teaching Criteria
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The aim of this study was to explore the evaluation methods of university teachers'effective teaching criteria with python programming. The evaluation criteria of 539 university teachers was carried out with a python programming Bayesian discriminant function. The results showed that: 1. The structure of effective teaching criteria for evaluation university teaching were student factors, teacher factors, teaching contents, teaching media, teaching environment, teaching evaluation and feedback evaluation process. 2. The overall evaluation of teachers' effective teaching and its sub dimensions were at the medium level. It showed that the teaching quality of the teachers need to be improved in general. 3. The teaching quality in the major of science and engineering was significantly higher than that of liberal arts and medicine, and no significant difference between liberal arts and medicine was found. This may partly be attributed to the nature of different subjects. 4.The higher the teacher's professional title was, the better the teaching quality was found. It suggested that the evaluation criteria of effective teaching about university teachers should take into account the teachers' qualities such as experience, knowledge, which were embedded in the term of “title”.

articleTitle: Microwave Ablation Treatment of Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Experience Sharing and Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is due to abnormal secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH) from parathyroid tissue.It acts on the bones, kidneys, and small intestine, causing systemic diseases such as calcium, phosphorus, and bone meta-bolic disorders. Surgery is the only effective treatment for PHPT. Some patients with PHPT cannot undergo surgical treatment due to surgical contraindications or failure to tolerate surgery. With the development of minimally invasive techniques, ethanol injection and thermal ablation treatment method have been reported, and have a good prognosis. Our hospital successfully applied microwave ablation technology to treat a patient with primary hyperparathyroidism. Parathyro-id tumors have a soft texture, mostly oblate, round cake-like, usually located on the dorsal side of the thyroid, adjacent to the nerve vessels, lacking a solid support around them. During the microwave ablation, glands are prone to retreat,at this time, we should pay attention to the operating range. In conjunction with liquid barriers, repeatedly piercing.When the ultrasound probe shows that the ablation needle has been punctured into the tumor, it is recommended that the operator press the ablation needle posteriorly to press the front end of the needle to try to keep it away from the recurrent laryngeal nerve. At the same time, due to the brittle and fragile texture of parathyroid tissue, in order to achieve a thorough effect of ablation, it is necessary to expand the scope of ablation as much as possible. Therefore, the range of ablation is suggested to include adjacent thyroid and fibrous connective tissue. The liquid barrier method allows the gland to be isolated from the major blood vessels and vital nerves of the neck, and at the same time absorbs heat from ablation, avoids heat injury to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, and reduces the risk of surgery and neck discomfort.The successful treatment of this patient showed that microwave ablation of PHPT is a safe and effective method. The technique is minimally invasive and does not require general anesthesia. It has lower requirements for patients' cardiopulmonary function and is especially suitable for elderly patients and patients with multiple organ diseases. At present, there are few reports on microwave ablation technology for the treatment of PHPT in China. There is no relevant report on the operation experience sharing in surgery. This article summarizes one case of microwave ablation technology for the successful treatment of PHPT for your reference.

articleTitle: Association Analysis of University Course Information Based on Knowledge Map
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In order to optimize educational decision-making and curriculum reform, trace the undergraduates' current development situation and forecast the follow-up study status, this paper adopts association rule algorithms to analyse the educational variables such as students' grades and curriculum selections information. The dataset referred in this paper is bigger, fresher, and more compound compared with the previous version. Based on those undergraduates' pre-existing data, pruning strategy is used to divide and process the dataset mathematically. By implementing modified Apriori algorithm, several significant association rules are dug out. In association rule mining, the Booleanized transaction data, optimized connection and pruning processing help us to find frequent item sets fleetly. Not only the dimension of the project set increases but also the efficiency of the modified algorithm are greatly improved. Through a rigorous survey of the experimental results, we carried out extensive analyses based on the heuristic knowledge of curriculum map. There is a certain degree of correlation hidden in the students' compulsory course scores. In the choice of public elective courses, some association rules related to the innate character of public elective courses are obtained. The analysis results provide fundamental basis for the construction of school public course map and the innovation of teaching method.

articleTitle: Case-Based Teaching Approach to Explore the Impact of Effective Questioning on the Teaching of "Toxicology"
publicationTitle: 2018 9th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective To explore the effect of effective questioning on the teaching of “Toxicology” based on case-based teaching, and to accumulate experience for further promoting the reform of Toxicology. Methods We selected 317 undergraduates of preventive medicine in Grade 2012, 2013 and 2014, from Shaanxi University of Chinese Medicine as research objects. Two teaching cases were planned in the instructional design for Grade 2012, while six teaching cases were planned for Grade 2013. The instructional design for Grade 2014 implemented effective questioning on the basis of Grade 2013. The difference in test paper scores, grade point average (GPA), the difficulty level of the test paper and grade were analyzed before and after the increase of case-based teaching and effective questioning. Results The test paper scores and grade point averages increased gradually from Grades 2012, 2013 and 2014, and the difference was statistically significant (F=99.722, P<;0.05; F=60.366, P<;0.05). The test paper scores and grade point averages of Grades 2013 and 2014 were significantly higher than those of Grade 2012 (P<;0.05), while those in Grade 2014 were higher than for Grade 2013 (P<;0.05).
